newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight orders cited, Brazil prominent.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight orders cited, Brazil prominent.

text.p: South Brazil again dominated business on London's sugar freight market at the start of the week, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Of the day's firmer business, Glencore fixed 22/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to the Mediterranean/Black Sea for prompt shipment.
Amerop fixed 27/28,500 tonnes from Thailand to US Gulf/Atlantic with west coast option for early July.
CSR was said to be open for a new 27,000-tonne bulk cargo from Queensland to Japan for prompt dates.

Shipbrokers said Fiji Sugar Marketing was open for 20,000 tonnes in bulk on its usual route from Fiji to London for 25 July/5 August and Mauritius Sugar for 18,000 tonnes from Port Louis to London for July 21/26.

Jean Lion quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to Mediterranean for prompt/10 days notice and Sugar Export was in for a prompt 13,500 tonnes from Imbituba to Dakar with options of Tema and Lagos.

Czarnikow Rionda was open for 24/30,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for July 1/15 and 4/7,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to Guayaquil for spot/prompt shipment.
Cargill was once again prominent in the day's new business, shipbrokers said.
It quoted for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Santos to Mombasa with options of Djibouti, Berbera, Yemen and Aqaba for any five days spot/21 July.
Cargill was also open for a 13,000-tonne min/max bagged cargo from Antwerp to Jeddah for July 11/16.
It issued two orders to Haiti, quoting for 3/3,300 tonnes in bulk from Puerto Quetzal for prompt/July 15 and 3,000 in bags from east coast Mexico for July 1/10.
Lastly, Cargill quoted for 11,500/20,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Corinto/Acajutla to US Gulf/Atlantic for July 1/10.

Lorico was open for 10,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rio de Janeiro to Egyptian Mediterranean for July 10/20 and Benham (or nominee) quoted for 4,600/4,700 tonnes in bulk from Taiwan to Crockett for July dates.
Shipbrokers said Louis Dreyfus was open for a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from Paranagua or Vitoria to Red Sea plus various options for July 12/16, or spot.

Secretan was open with a couple of bagged account orders, quoting for 12,500/13,000 tonnes from Santos or Paranagua to east Africa/Red Sea for July 7/15 and 6,000 tonnes from Durban to Maputo/Dar es Salaam for July 5/10.
Shyvers Savoy quoted an account order for 11,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Puerto Cabello for July 10/15.

Genoc was seeking tonnage for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar in loose or preslung bags from Santos, Paranagua or Rio de Janeiro to Mediterranean with a large range of options for prompt with 14 days notice.
These were Black Sea, Red Sea and Arabian Gulf including Iraq, east Africa and Indian Ocean.
Genoc also quoted for 3/7,000 tonnes of bagged sugar, possibly as a part-cargo, for July shipment dates.

In other news, French dockers staged a one-day strike on Monday to protest over inadequate pay. The largest ports of Le Havre and Marseille were hit, as were nine others including Calais, Boulogne and Cherbourg.
-- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
